title: Prediction of Academic Performance: Use of ICT at Home and School and Cyberbullying
content: Introduction: Post-pandemic, there has been significant investment in Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in schools worldwide. Recent studies show a negative link between academic performance and issues like bullying and cyberbullying. Objective: This study aims to analyze and predict the relationship between PISA 2022 performance and bullying, cyberbullying, and ICT use at school and home in high (Level 6) and low (Level 1a) performance students. Methodology: A non-experimental, descriptive study using the PISA 2022 questionnaire. Participants: 613,744 students. Variables include: (i) Independent: (a) Bullying and cyberbullying (1–16 scale), (b) ICT use at school (1–7 scale), (c) ICT use at home (1–6 scale). (ii) Dependent: Scores in mathematics, reading, and science. Performance was dichotomized into: (i) Level 1a vs. Non-Level 1a (scores below 335 in Science and Reading, 358 in Math) and (ii) Level 6 vs. Non-Level 6 (scores above 708 in Science, 698 in Reading, 669 in Math). Data Analysis: Binary logistic regression was used to predict high performance based on predictors: (a) Bullying and cyberbullying, (b) ICT availability at school and home. Results: Online distress and cyberbullying increase the risk of low performance, with greater impact on low performers. Conclusion: Distress from online content and cyberbullying is a risk factor for academic performance. ICT access at home benefits academic results, while ICT use at school has varied effects depending on the subject.
